text:
### Observed differences

- A02 disappeared. In the earlier window it ran in 46 in 100 traces — at most once per trace, at a median position about 0.11 into the trace — and its observed outgoing transitions went mainly to A03 (about 32%), A06 (about 22%) and A11 (about 14%). In the later window it is absent from all 200 traces and shows no outgoing transitions. [OCC002, POS002, DIR002]
- A01 appeared where A02 used to be. It was not observed before; in the later window it runs in about 51 in 100 traces, once per trace, at a median position about 0.14 into the trace. The two activities never occur together in either window: before, 46 in 100 traces contained A02 without A01; after, about 51 in 100 contain A01 without A02. [OCC001, POS001, REL001]
- A01's routing resembles A02's. Of A01's observed outgoing transitions in the later window, about 24% lead to A06 and 19% to A03, with A10 and A11 next (about 15% each); before, A02's outgoing transitions led mainly to A03 (about 32%), A06 (about 22%), A11 (about 14%) and A13 (about 11%). [DIR001, DIR002]
- The relations to neighbouring activities carried over. With A03: before, A02 co-occurred with A03 in 46 in 100 traces in a mixed order (A03 first in about 17, A02 first in about 12, interleaved in about 18 per 100 traces); after, A01 co-occurs with A03 in about 51 in 100 traces, again in mixed order (A03 first about 20, interleaved about 26, A01 first about 5). A03 itself runs in every trace in both windows. With A06: before, A02 co-occurred with A06 in 26 in 100 traces, usually with A02 first (about 16); after, A01 co-occurs with A06 in about 26 in 100 traces, with A01 first in about 11 and interleaved in about 13. A06's own participation is roughly stable (about 53 in 100 traces before, 50 in 100 after). [REL002, REL004, REL005, REL003]
- A03's outgoing edges show the same swap: the transition to A02 (about 7% of A03's outgoing transitions before) is gone, and a transition to A01 (about 8%) is now observed. A03's remaining shares shifted only modestly (to A10 up from about 32% to 37%, to A11 down from about 24% to 19%). [DIR003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A01 took over the role previously played by A02: A02 was removed, and A01 now runs in its place — in a similar share of traces (about 51 in 100 vs 46 in 100), around the same position in the trace, at most once per trace, followed by the same main successors (A06 and A03), and keeping the same mixed-order co-occurrence with A03 and the predominantly A-first co-occurrence with A06. The support is direct and consistent: participation and position items show the symmetric disappearance and appearance, the successor distribution of A01 in the later window matches A02's earlier one, the A03→A02 edge became A03→A01, and twelve control-flow items qualified where only about 0.21 would be expected by chance across the 43 tested units — far more than an unchanged process typically produces. [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, POS002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]

Limitations: the two windows are separate samples, so the two activities are never observed together and equivalence in purpose cannot be shown directly; positions are event ranks, not clock times. A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is that A02 was simply dropped and A01 added as a different step that happens to sit in the same region of the process near A03 and A06 — the matching routing and relation profiles make this less plausible but do not exclude it. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, REL002]

Other differences: the slight redistribution of A03's remaining outgoing shares (more to A10, fewer to A11) is a minor redistribution not part of the substitution hypothesis. [DIR003]
